milestone: First clean full run in 26 hours (since R48 at 10:37 previous day). All quality gates pass. First duo run in session with non-zero swap (5.48 GB). First duo run where 16K prefill fell BELOW the 500 tok/s Goal 4 floor under co-tenancy (475.6 tok/s).

pre_run.note: Best pre-run conditions since R48 — sustained calm (1m/5m/15m all ~2.3)

post_run.note: Load dropped further during the run — engineer workload finished while bench ran

speed_metrics.goal_4_status: MISSED at 16K: 475.6 tok/s < 500 target. First duo run in session below the Goal 4 16K floor. R44/R47/R48 all reported 502 here. The 26 tok/s drop is correlated with co-tenancy: RULER 3b phase time was 301s vs R44 237s (+27%), MMLU-Pro 912s vs 907s (+0.6% — this phase is less co-tenancy sensitive).
speed_metrics.goal_4_status_4k: MET at 4K: 801.1 tok/s (identical to R47 803). The 4K path is immune to co-tenancy pressure.
speed_metrics.goal_3_status: Decode 29.6 @ 4K (-15% vs R47 34.8, -17% vs R44 34.9). This is the first duo run in session with <30 tok/s 4K decode. Under the clean-box 50 tok/s Goal 3 target (59% of target). The drop happened entirely between R48 and R59 — same code, different co-tenancy — confirming the decode path is bandwidth-bound and very sensitive to memory pressure.

memory.swap_peak_note: FIRST non-zero swap peak in the duo session (R44/R47/R48 all 0.0 GB). 5.48 GB is 42% of the 12.9 GB watchdog limit — well within Goal 5 gate but materially different from the maximum-headroom runs recorded earlier.

swap_io_mb_per_s.max_anomaly_note: Max of 2678 MB/s is an instantaneous spike that exceeds the M4 Pro's advertised 430 MB/s swap bandwidth ceiling. This is almost certainly a sampler artifact — psutil's swap-io calculation divides a raw byte count by a small elapsed-time interval, and if the sampler was paged out itself for part of that interval the effective-Δt is tiny. The p90 metric is the reliable gate; max is noise.

goal_5_p90: 15.8 MB/s PASS — but notably HIGHER than R44/R47/R48 which were all 0.0 p90. This run is closer to the Goal 5 edge than any duo run before it. The pattern: co-tenancy drives real swap I/O that didn't exist in the clean-box runs.

comparison_to_prior_duo_runs.interpretation: R44-R48 were clean-box runs (0.0 swap, Goal 4 16K MET at 502). R58 was a co-tenancy crash (watchdog fired). R59 is the middle case: co-tenancy present but below the breach threshold. Quality gates still pass, but Goal 4 16K prefill MISSES the floor by 24 tok/s and decode drops 15%. This establishes that the Goal 3/4/5 numbers reported for the default duo path in CLAUDE.md are clean-box-only.

intervening_commits_since_run58.note: Working SHA advanced from c643046 (R58 commit) to 25be876. Commits in between include engineer test/fix work. Not enumerated here — see git log c643046..25be876 for details.

analyst_observations.co_tenancy_is_the_story_of_this_session: Runs 44/47/48 were clean-box, 58 was over-the-edge, 59 is the calibration point showing the duo path under moderate co-tenancy. Five different pressure scenarios with the SAME code path producing measurably different results. This is exactly the kind of data that distinguishes empirical performance claims from synthetic bench claims.
analyst_observations.claude_md_should_note_the_clean_box_cave: The current CLAUDE.md Goal 3/4/5 status rows say 'MET' with specific numbers (52.4 tok/s decode, 803/501 prefill, zero swap). R59 under normal co-tenancy measures 29.6/475.6/5.48 — materially different. The goals are still empirically true on a clean box, but a reader glancing at CLAUDE.md would not know that. Worth a one-line qualifier on each row.
analyst_observations.no_new_task_filed: This analysis doesn't need a new TASKS.md entry because: (a) Task #85 covers watchdog log flushing, (b) Task #86 covers per-phase headroom check which would SKIP Phase 3 NIAH 16K under co-tenancy pressure, making the 475.6 tok/s a moot data point, (c) Task #80 covers profiler wall-clock correlation which would flag the co-tenancy slowdown. The three already-filed tasks together address every observation in R59 — the analyst doesn't need to pile on more tasks for the same finding class.
